newsitem.title: PUERTO RICO: Puerto Rico seeks to sell off govt-held phone firm.
newsitem.headline: Puerto Rico seeks to sell off govt-held phone firm.

text.p: Puerto Rico will seek to sell off the government-owned Puerto Rico Telephone Company, Gov. Pedro Rossello said Monday.

Rossello told a news conference he had ordered Government Development Bank President Marcos Rodriguez Ema, who heads the government's privatization efforts, to begin the sale process but gave few other details.

Proceeds from the planned sale would be used for infrastructure investment, to capitalize the retirement system for public employees, and to create a benefits scheme for current employees of the firm, which includes a wireless telephone and beeper division.
The government sold the long-distance arm of the firm in 1992 for $142 million to Telefonica Internacional, a unit of Telefonica de Espana.
Rossello said the government was taking the measure because the company faces increased competition from private firms in the local market following the loss of its monopoly last year.
